questiontext.text: In a binary expression tree, what do the internal nodes and leaves represent?

answer.text: Internal nodes are operators; leaves are operands

feedback.text: Correct — operators combine the results of their operand subtrees.

answer.text: Internal nodes are operands; leaves are operators

feedback.text: No — it is the reverse: operators are internal, operands are leaves.

answer.text: Every node holds both an operator and an operand

feedback.text: No — each node is one or the other.
No — operators must appear at internal nodes.

generalfeedback.text: An expression tree places operators at internal nodes and operands (constants or variables) at the leaves.

questiontext.text: Which traversal of an expression tree yields the postfix (RPN) form of the expression?

feedback.text: Correct — visiting both subtrees before the operator produces postfix.
No — pre-order (operator first) gives prefix notation.
No — in-order gives infix (needs parentheses to be unambiguous).
No — a breadth-first walk does not correspond to a standard notation.

generalfeedback.text: Post-order visits left, right, then root, so operators follow their operands — exactly postfix / RPN.

questiontext.text: An in-order traversal of an expression tree (with parentheses) produces which notation?

feedback.text: Correct — the operator appears between its operands, the usual infix form.
No — postfix comes from post-order.
No — prefix comes from pre-order.
No — traversal order does not produce machine code.

generalfeedback.text: In-order visits left subtree, root, right subtree, so the operator sits between its operands — infix (parentheses restore precedence).

questiontext.text: To evaluate an expression tree, which recursive strategy is natural?

answer.text: Post-order: evaluate both subtrees, then apply the operator

feedback.text: Correct — operand values must be ready before the operator is applied.

answer.text: Pre-order: apply the operator before evaluating subtrees

feedback.text: No — the operator needs its operands' values first.
No — a breadth-first pass does not respect operand dependencies.
No — both operands are required.

generalfeedback.text: Evaluation recurses post-order: compute the left value, compute the right value, then combine them with the node's operator.

questiontext.text: A pre-order traversal of an expression tree produces prefix (Polish) notation.

feedback.text: Correct — visiting the operator before its operands gives prefix.
Pre-order visits root first, which is exactly prefix notation.

questiontext.text: In a binary expression tree, operators are stored at the leaf nodes.

feedback.text: No — operators are internal nodes; leaves hold operands.
Correct — operators are internal; operands are at the leaves.
